title: Perplexity Comet Pricing for Free, Pro and Max Plans
summary: Perplexity Comet pricing in 2026 includes free and paid tiers. Compare feature sets and costs across all subscription options to find your fit.
body_markdown:
## Automate repeat Comet tasks with Activepieces


If the job is one you keep handing to a browser agent every week, it probably belongs in a workflow instead of an agent run.


### Comet tasks better run as workflows


### Why repeat tasks fail in Comet's agent


Most teams find this out by accident. Someone asks the agent to check competitor pricing pages on Monday, then again the next Monday, and soon it's a ritual nobody owns.


Each run spends agent usage on the same steps, and each run can wander differently: a changed layout, a cookie banner, a page read slightly differently.


Handing a task you repeat on a fixed rhythm with a fixed shape to the most flexible and most metered tool you have is a poor use of it.


Run one test: **if you can write the steps down** in advance, the agent is paying for judgment the task never needs.


### Benefits of workflows over Comet agent runs


Because **a workflow runs the same path every time** , the bill is predictable and a failure shows up at a named step instead of somewhere inside a long agent session.


It also lets you grant each step only the access it needs, which is the least-privilege problem solved by design rather than by a policy line.


The browser agent sits beside it for one-off tasks.


Take from it that the recurring path and the exploratory path are different jobs, and each gets its own tool.


Once the recurring work is out of the agent, what remains is the work that genuinely needs one.


### Running automated workflows on schedule


Activepieces is an automation platform that builds this kind of flow: a trigger, a series of steps, an AI step in the middle, and integrations at the end. You set the schedule once, and it runs without anyone opening a browser.


Its published pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, however many steps the run has, whereas Zapier's per-task billing on its own pricing page counts each step separately.


So the weekly fetch, summarise and post flow costs one credit, the same as a two-step version of it.


You don't need it. That holds when the task is truly one-off, when the steps change each time, or when a single scheduled prompt in a tool you already pay for does the job.
